summary:
Summer Fuels Outlook
Light At the End of the Tunnel EIA Short-Term Energy and Summer Fuels Outlook The US Energy Information Agency (EIA) has just released the Short‐Term Energy and Summer Fuels Outlook providing a taste of what can be expected through 2010; lower crude oil demand and lower petroleum prices in the short term until the global economic engine kicks back into gear in 2010. A year ago, the tanker market was on the verge of experiencing one of the most volatile summers in history, crude oil prices were about to embark on a major climb and the effects of the Beijing Olympics on oil demand were being hotly debated. A year later, with the memories of robust times fading, the EIA is predicting the West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil price to average $54/bbl this summer as compared to its forecast for last summer of $97/bbl.

children.title: China
children.summary: US Other World The EIA projects crude oil consumption in the Organization for Economic Co‐Operation and Development (OECD) countries to fall by 1.6 million barrels per day (bbls/day) while Non‐ OECD growth is predicted to increase by 270,000 bbls/day - yielding a net decrease in demand of roughly 1.3 million bbls/day. By the end of 2009 and into the first quarter of 2010, the EIA is expecting economic recovery pushing world crude oil consumption up by 1.1 million bbls/day from 2009's projected level of 84 million bbls/day.

children.title: Hitting the Summer Pavement
children.summary: The Summer Fuels Outlook highlights the obvious changes in market conditions from 2008 to 2009, but more importantly how lower crude oil prices resulting impact on consumer demand will affect refined product yields. The chart below shows historical and projected US retail gasoline and diesel prices.

children.title: Diesel Price
children.summary: Gasoline Price Keeping in theme with crude oil expectations, the EIA expects prices to be significantly lower than last summer. Moreover, the margins refiners captured on diesel last summer are likely to diminish.

children.title: Blinded by the Light
children.summary: The EIA projects that global demand for crude oil will continue to be soft until the economic recovery in 2010 reinvigorates worldwide industrial growth and consumer spending. Although the outlook provides plenty of food for thought, actions at the pump will ultimately speak louder than words.
